liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Looks Like Rain** (3 reviews): Thunder effects in Looks Like Rain can strain weaker speakers, especially with a woofer; Reviewer had never heard the band use thunder sound effects on Looks Like Rain before; sounds great [25][27][30]
- **Playing In The Band** (2 reviews): Second-set Crazy Fingers, Playin', Uncle John's, Playin' stretch is high-energy with prominent Phil bass; Reviewer says it was the only Playin' > Uncle John's > Playin' sandwich they ever witnessed [20][30]
- **One Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Feel Like A Stranger is described as well jammed [21]
- **Me And My Uncle** (1 review): Me and My Uncle into Cumberland Blues is well done [29]
- **Far From Me** (1 review): Far From Me is a passionate rendition [29]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): Cassidy on this recording is called absolutely velvet [24]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): Smooth, slow and jazzy; Jerry watched Brent throughout, the two playing off each other, likened to 10/20/74 [23]

## Setlist highlights

- **deadspace**: rare: 3 archived performances [32]
- **Bill Graham's goodnight**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [32]

## The recordings

- **gd90-06-23.sbd.ladner.28690.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 23 songs; 170 min; rated 4.74/5 by 34 [1]. Said about its sound: Considered one of the best-sounding 1990 recordings; Thick, bass-heavy recording that captures the sound of that summer; Phil's bombs come through strongly; Mix and recording are stellar; the music pops [24][25][29]
- **gd1990-06-23.aud.ladner.10261.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 21 songs; 171 min; rated 3/5 by 2 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer suspects a Healy matrix source; audience audible in the mix and the sound is somewhat flat [20]
- **gd1990-06-23.156400.mtx.photoleon.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 178 min [8]
- **gd1990-06-23.163867.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 21 songs; 170 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [9]
- **gd1990-06-23.akg-nak.miller.99648.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 168 min; rated 2.67/5 by 3 [18]

## Around the show

- Eugene felt hospitable, the stadium wasn't too huge, and the crowd was loving it; reviewer's favorite shows of the year [22]
- Reviewer stood fifth row center and recalls Jerry looking toward Brent during Eyes [23]
- Bill Graham handed out garbage bags in the parking lot; the afternoon in Oregon was sunny [30]
- Reviewer's 21st birthday; it was the largest venue they saw the band play, and they lived in Eugene [31]
- Taper recorded from front row center of the tapers' section with the mic stand about 8-9 feet high [18]
- Reviewer ranks the two Eugene shows as the best representation of the band at its 1990 peak [21]
- Feels looser and more atmospheric than the technically precise playing of spring 1990 [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd90-06-23.sbd.ladner.28690.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD-matrix>CM>DAT>CDR>WAV>SHN - see info file for more details. Upgrade over previous SBD source. [1]. Also: Described as an upgrade over the earlier soundboard source [1]
- **gd1990-06-23.aud.ladner.10261.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD>Cm>Dat>Samplitude>CD. Seeded by Charlie Miller via Neo_Levo to candyman and abgd. [6]
- **gd1990-06-23.156400.mtx.photoleon.flac16**: source: Matrix created in Adobe Audition by Joe Noel November 24, 2021 [8]. Also: Soundboard recording credited to Don Pearson and Dan Healy; Charlie Miller did the transfers; Dave Brotman supplied the spaced front-of-board recording; other sources patch the opening of set one and parts of set two [8]
- **gd1990-06-23.163867.nak700.severson.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Mark Severson; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Mark Severson's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D6 [9]. Also: A Schoeps CMC4 MK21 source from Ted Mattes supplies a ten-second patch in Uncle John's Band [9]
- **gd1990-06-23.akg-nak.miller.99648.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Charlie Miller; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Nakamichi 100/CP4 + AKG C1000S -> Boss BX-4 -> Cassette Master (Sony WM-D6C) -> Cassette [18]. Also: Sennheiser ME-80 recording to DAT, a four-mic mix, supplies one minute of Uncle John's Band; Taper's masters were lost; the patch comes from a poor first-generation tape needing heavy pitch correction [18]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by gocollect.com: [Grateful Dead & Little Feat Autzen Stadium Fan Art 1990 Value - GoCollect](https://gocollect.com/concert-poster/grateful-dead-autzen-stadium-1990) [33]
- Fan art by Jerry Garcia: [1990-06-23 Autzen Stadium, U. of Oregon, Eugene, OR, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1990-06-23-autzen-stadium-u-of-oregon-eugene-or-usa/) [34]
- Fan art by RareVinyl.com: [Grateful Dead Dave's Picks, Volume 44 (Autzen Stadium, U. Of Oregon, Eugene, OR 6/23/90) - Sealed 2022 US 3-CD set](https://uk.rarevinyl.com/products/grateful-dead-dave-s-picks-volume-44-autzen-stadium-u-of-oregon-eugene-or-6-23-90-sealed-us-3-cd-album-triple-set-r2677184-847515) [35]

claims.text: Reviewer suspects a Healy matrix source; audience audible in the mix and the sound is somewhat flat
Second-set Crazy Fingers, Playin', Uncle John's, Playin' stretch is high-energy with prominent Phil bass
Reviewer ranks the two Eugene shows as the best representation of the band at its 1990 peak
Feel Like A Stranger is described as well jammed
Eugene felt hospitable, the stadium wasn't too huge, and the crowd was loving it; reviewer's favorite shows of the year
Smooth, slow and jazzy; Jerry watched Brent throughout, the two playing off each other, likened to 10/20/74
Reviewer stood fifth row center and recalls Jerry looking toward Brent during Eyes
Cassidy on this recording is called absolutely velvet
Considered one of the best-sounding 1990 recordings
Thick, bass-heavy recording that captures the sound of that summer; Phil's bombs come through strongly
Thunder effects in Looks Like Rain can strain weaker speakers, especially with a woofer
Feels looser and more atmospheric than the technically precise playing of spring 1990
Reviewer had never heard the band use thunder sound effects on Looks Like Rain before; sounds great
Mix and recording are stellar; the music pops
Far From Me is a passionate rendition
Me and My Uncle into Cumberland Blues is well done
Bill Graham handed out garbage bags in the parking lot; the afternoon in Oregon was sunny
Ken Kesey arrived in his new bus and played the Thunder Machine during this song
Reviewer says it was the only Playin' > Uncle John's > Playin' sandwich they ever witnessed
Reviewer's 21st birthday; it was the largest venue they saw the band play, and they lived in Eugene
Source chain: soundboard matrix, then CM, DAT, CDR, WAV, SHN
Described as an upgrade over the earlier soundboard source
Soundboard recording credited to Don Pearson and Dan Healy; Charlie Miller did the transfers
Dave Brotman supplied the spaced front-of-board recording; other sources patch the opening of set one and parts of set two
Mark Severson supplied master cassettes; Charlie Miller transferred them and coordinated the release
A Schoeps CMC4 MK21 source from Ted Mattes supplies a ten-second patch in Uncle John's Band
Sennheiser ME-80 recording to DAT, a four-mic mix, supplies one minute of Uncle John's Band
Taper recorded from front row center of the tapers' section with the mic stand about 8-9 feet high
Taper's masters were lost; the patch comes from a poor first-generation tape needing heavy pitch correction
